title: Retagging identifies the normalized diagonal orientation on coordinate charts
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q\subset k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$, with the small pro-etale conventions [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes with structural maps $a_X,a_Y$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Fix an automorphism $\sigma:k\simeq k$ fixing $k_0$. For $T=X,Y$ put $T^\sigma=(T,\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\circ a_T)$ and let $f^\sigma:X^\sigma\to Y^\sigma$ be the same underlying scheme morphism. Identify the small sites, constant coefficient sheaves and Tate lines [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] by the identity of underlying schemes. Use the same underlying compactification to identify compact-support direct images, and use the unique counit-preserving isomorphisms to identify their constructible right adjoints [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

For $m\geq1$ put $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^m$, using $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and uniformizer $\ell$. Let $V\subseteq Y$ be an affine open, let $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ be open, write $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and suppose $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_V$ is an etale $V$-morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. Write $\Pi_{f,R}:Rf_R^!R_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X(d)[2d]$ and $\Pi_{f^\sigma,R}$ for the normalized diagonal orientations [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. Then
$$Lj^*\Pi_{f^\sigma,R}=Lj^*\Pi_{f,R}.$$
More precisely, the identity of underlying schemes identifies the relative diagonals $X\hookrightarrow X\times_YX$, their normal bundles, and the deformation families of [def-pur-dnc-section-family], including their fibres at $0,1$, punctured trivializations and etale coordinate maps. Under the corresponding identity and counit-preserving identifications of section invariants [def-pur-section-invariant], it identifies the normalized diagonal-to-normal-bundle comparisons [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] on these charts, as well as the integration-normalized vector-bundle orientations [det-sp-orientation-vector-bundle]. The equality displayed above is an equality of derived morphisms under the coordinate-adjunction identifications of [det-sp-orientation-charts], with the Tate-line normalization and its power transition maps retained.

proof.text: The defining normalization in thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object depends on aY only through proofs of Noetherianity and invertibility of the fixed coefficient exponent. All these witnesses lie in Prop. Thus the ordinary witness extracted from the normalized orientation for one structure map satisfies exactly the normalization for any other finite-type structure map on the same underlying base. The pro-etale comparison uses the same compactification, because HasCompactification is a proposition. Apply the uniqueness clause to identify the two actual diagonal isomorphisms. Congruence under the derived pullback along U gives the first required equality, without needing chart descent again. This includes empty charts and d=0.

source.place: Step 1; auxiliary retagging argument, using the published coordinate normalization and DNC uniqueness

proof.text: The underlying extended-Rees source, projection and augmentation in def-pur-dnc-section-family are definitionally unchanged by postcomposing the structural map. The finite section invariant and family use the same actual underlying maps and coefficient object; their compactifiability witnesses are proofs. The normal section object and both fibre comparisons of lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry likewise have only proof-irrelevant dependence on the structural map. Reflexivity proves their heterogeneous equalities for the relative diagonal, which is the same closed section of the same pullback projection.

source.place: Step 1; auxiliary retagging argument, using the published coordinate normalization and DNC uniqueness

proof.text: Let alpha_sigma be the chosen DNC isomorphism for the retagged base. For every original test base (Bprime,aBprime) and b with b composed with aB equal to aBprime, postcompose that equation with Spec(sigma). The same b is then a morphism of the retagged bases. Evaluate the normalization of alpha_sigma on (Bprime,aBprime composed with Spec(sigma)), the same C0 and the same family trivialization e. All underlying family, source and normal comparison maps agree definitionally. Hence alpha_sigma satisfies the original normalization predicate. The uniqueness clause of thm-pur-dnc-invariance identifies it with the original chosen isomorphism.

source.place: Step 1; auxiliary retagging argument, using the published coordinate normalization and DNC uniqueness

proof.text: For every vector-bundle presentation of the normal bundle, apply det-sp-orientation-vector-bundle to each of the two structural maps. These give both actual integration-transpose equations required in RetaggingVectorOrientationConclusion. The general structure-independence argument of Step 1 identifies their hom arrows. The geometric affine and smooth projection facts in that same vector-bundle interface discharge the domain hypotheses. No arbitrary orientation or frame is chosen.

source.place: Step 1; auxiliary retagging argument, using the published coordinate normalization and DNC uniqueness

proof.text: Over.map of the field automorphism keeps the underlying scheme definitionally equal to the original scheme. The pro-etale roots-of-unity tower of def-coefficient-twists-detailed is a construction on that underlying scheme alone; reflexivity identifies the entire tower, including its power transitions. Combine this equality and the preceding three clauses to obtain the unchanged conclusion.
